feedback.title: Audit the feedback entries
feedback.imperative: Read the AGENT_FEEDBACK entries for this run/epic. Extract candidates from friction, adherence deviations, and improvement signals. Weight friction the run worked around over friction merely asserted.
feedback.finding: Six AGENT_FEEDBACK entries read (harvest-226/227,228,229,230,231,232). Cross-cutting frictions beyond what logs already surfaced: (1) checklist_engine.py's negation-wrapper pattern -- #229's implementer improvised '! <command>' to make a command-postcondition prove a guard CORRECTLY FAILS, since the engine's command-postcondition semantics assume exit0=pass; banked as lesson:prove-command-fails-postcondition (handoff scope, 1 data point). (2) #229: harness Agent-tool run_in_background/name params unavailable this session ('flat team roster') -- same class as #227's finding, TWO independent data points same epic. (3) #229: py launcher resolves to a sandboxed codex-runtime lacking pytest/coverage pre-installed -- adjacent to but not merged with #228's py-resolution finding. (4) #228 continuation commander: taking over a stalled predecessor requires reclaiming TWO independent engine leases (parent spine + any in-progress nested survey child checklist), not one -- worth naming explicitly in continuation-commander dispatch instructions. (5) #230: attest refuses engine-checked postconditions only after you try -- current does not distinguish attestable from engine-checked postconditions, costing one wasted call per gate; also exported to CONSTELLATION_FEEDBACK with a concrete fix (current --conditions flag showing check kind per condition). (6) #230 CONSTELLATION_FEEDBACK item 4: 'canonical-routing-can-dissolve-a-file-fence' -- a launch-order stop-condition ('float if another wave's PR touches this file') fired on an edit that PR-6 canonical-source routing made unnecessary; commander-230 resolved without blocking, saved a full Admiral round-trip. (7) #232: attach --payload-file requires JSON but crew artifacts (IMPLEMENTER_RESULT/REVIEW_RESULT) are Markdown by template convention -- undocumented constraint discovered via JSONDecodeError traceback; workaround (--field pointer-plus-summary) is arguably the correct 'return thin write fat' shape anyway but isn't named as such anywhere. (8) #232: --why/--note string containing backtick-wrapped code identifiers triggers Git-Bash command substitution through the harness's Bash tool, silently dropping the backticked word from the recorded digest even though the engine call succeeds -- a shell/harness interaction, not a doctrine gap. (9) #232 g2-review caught a Commander-authored map-anchor line-number drift WITHIN the same run (not across runs) as an earlier gate in the SAME run edited the file -- narrower case than the existing verify-launch-order-claims-against-code lesson, which is about trusting a prior RUN's claims; this is same-run same-gate-boundary drift.

telemetry.imperative: Cross-check candidates against telemetry: rework_count per task, BLOCK verdicts, waives/forced overrides, re-dispatches, incident counts. Mark each candidate corroborated or assertion-only; raise confidence only with corroboration.
telemetry.finding: Corroboration pass: (1) execute-the-advice-a-test-asserts-on -- HARD telemetry: execute.json g3-implement rework_count=3/3 (AT the cap; a 4th would have escalated per commander-227 sec 7), 3 sequential BLOCK verdicts across rework rounds 1-3, each a DIFFERENT symptom of the same fixture-blindness cause. Strongest-corroborated candidate in the whole audit. (2) verify-launch-order-claims-against-code -- 4 confirm ops now on file (152, 154 pre-epic + wt-227, wt-230 this epic) across 3 different epics/issues, 3 distinct failure shapes (already-shipped mechanism x2, named-target-does-not-exist x1, unnamed-token-pair x1) -- recurrence-with-variation is stronger corroboration than repeated identical hits. (3) sibling fork -- corroborated by two INDEPENDENT lessons-delta.json add ops in the SAME wave (harvest-226/228 and harvest-226/231), not merely asserted by the Admiral's narrative; Admiral's own RULING entry cross-referenced both files by path before ruling. (4) round-trip-tests-prove-artifacts-not-parsers -- corroborated by two INCIDENT-adjacent findings: #230's grade_lint silent-PASS+false-FAIL (both real bugs live through 18 passing tests until adversarial fixtures were demanded) and #227's Inv3ExclusionCheck undercoverage caught in g3 REVIEW ROUND 3 (i.e. it survived rounds 1-2 of the SAME rework loop that was hunting exactly this class of defect) -- BLOCK-verdict-adjacent, not assertion-only. (5) Write-tool findings-filename refusal -- corroborated by 2 independent INCIDENT-class hits (cmd-227's crew, commander-231) in the same epic, zero content lost either time (workaround always available) -- real but low-severity, capped at medium confidence since it is a harness policy the repo cannot fix. (6) prove-command-fails-postcondition -- ASSERTION-ONLY, 1 data point, no BLOCK/rework attached; stays banked, not corroborated for graduation this audit. (7) cold-critic-mandatory-for-measurement-plans -- ASSERTION-ONLY from 2 commanders' prose, but indirectly corroborated: #230's cold critic caught BLOCKER 1 (a grammar undefined that would have broken the issue's OWN required round-trip test) and #227's cold critic caught the same-shape 'baseline unproducible after g1/g2 overwrites the engine' defect -- both are pre-crew catches of defects that would otherwise have surfaced only after rework rounds were spent, i.e. avoided-rework is the telemetry signal even though no counterfactual rework count exists to cite directly. (8) Two ADMIRAL ERRORs -- self-reported, uncorroborated by independent telemetry (no second agent caught either one) but both are Admiral's own INCIDENT-grade log entries with a stated cost, which this audit treats as equivalent-weight to a corroborated crew finding per 'own errors in the open' doctrine.

### Harvest-before-sweep is stated in doctrine but not mechanically checked, and it failed for real (0cc4eefd032c)
- occurrences: 1 across 1 project(s): f1Brainz
- observed: after this audit's first pass closed, team-lead found that all six fenced-commander
trios under `.agent-work/staged-feedback/` (624-phase0, 625-segmentation-substrate, wave4-626,
627-unified-basis, 638-f12-stability-rework, 630-phase6-bt-injection) had been **collected** out

dir) but **never merged** into the durable `.agent-work/AGENT_FEEDBACK.md` /
`CONSTELLATION_FEEDBACK.md`. All six source worktrees were already swept by closeout — the staging
directory was the sole surviving copy. Only Ship I/#513 (which wrote the durable files directly,
no fencing exception in play) had actually reached the durable log. Team-lead merged all 12 entries
by hand with provenance comments; `verify_agent_feedback.py --phase feedback` now passes.

`constellation-admiral/SKILL.md` Closeout step 4 already states this almost exactly —
*"Harvest first, **then** remove — a worktree swept before its trio is collected silently drops
that run's learning"* — so the doctrine text is not the gap. What's missing is **enforcement**:
nothing actually checks, before a `git worktree remove`, that every `staged-feedback/<work-id>/`
directory's content has landed in the durable files it's staged a copy of. Passing the fenced
commander's own `feedback`/`archive` gate (which verifies only the *staging* copy) reads as
"harvested," and looks identical to "harvested and merged" from the outside
- proposal: extend `verify_agent_feedback.py` (or add a sibling check) with a harvest-completeness
mode: for every `.agent-work/staged-feedback/<work-id>/` directory still present at closeout time,
confirm its `AGENT_FEEDBACK.md`/`CONSTELLATION_FEEDBACK.md` content (or a harvest-provenance marker
citing it) actually appears in the corresponding durable file, and refuse/warn `git worktree remove`
for that work-id's worktree until it does. This turns "collected" and "merged" back into one
checkable act instead of two acts that look identical from the outside
- grounding: `.agent-work/epic-601/ADMIRAL_LOG.md` Closeout section, INCIDENT + FIX entry dated
2026-07-24; `constellation-admiral/SKILL.md` Closeout step 4; direct inspection of
`.agent-work/staged-feedback/*/` (all six trios present, all six source worktrees confirmed absent
from `git worktree list` at the time of the finding)
- confidence: high (mechanically confirmed: 6/6 staged trios were absent from the durable log
